free_tier.stated: keyless JSON lookups of any public IPv4 or IPv6 address at https://ipkit.dev/{ip}: 300 requests per 60 seconds per caller IP address, no key; location, ASN, organisation and VPN, proxy and Tor flags from an upstream Ipregistry key held by the operator
free_tier.notes: the limit applies to current-IP and arbitrary lookups; no SLA or uptime promise is published.

per_object_cap.stated: one IP address per request (GET /{ip}); private and reserved ranges answer HTTP 400 RESERVED_IP

retention.stated: not applicable: a lookup API; specific-IP answers carry cache-control max-age=300 at the caller and s-maxage=3600 at the edge

egress.terms: not applicable: JSON answers, not metered in bytes

interface_detail: GET or HEAD https://ipkit.dev/{ip} and /api/ip/{ip} answer ipkit.v1 JSON; GET /api/my-ip answers for the caller; OPTIONS answers CORS preflight with 204
tooling: any HTTP client; branch on the HTTP status and the ipkit.v1 object
chaining: A keyless front end to Ipregistry data (source ipregistry) at 300 lookups a minute per caller IP, for scripts that need location, ASN and privacy flags with no account. Bulk path: none in the HTTP API.

limits.value: 300 requests per 60 seconds per caller IP address; HTTP 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After 60

binding_note: the per-minute limit per caller IP is the only published cap; arbitrary lookups also depend on one operator-held upstream key and answer HTTP 503 LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE without it.
reliability_note: no SLA or uptime promise is published; arbitrary lookups need the operator's upstream key and answer HTTP 503 LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE when it is missing; past the limit the API answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After 60
confidence_note: A keyless lookup of 8.8.8.8 was probed on 2026-11-02 and returned HTTP 200 with source ipregistry; the 300 requests per 60 seconds limit is quoted from the documentation and was not exhausted.

evidence.quote: There is no published SLA; use the service reasonably.

evidence.proved: the limit is 300 requests per 60 seconds per connecting IP
evidence.quote: Lookups are limited to 300 requests per 60 seconds per connecting client IP. The limit applies to current-IP and arbitrary lookups.

evidence.proved: HTTP 429 RATE_LIMITED is the answer past the limit
evidence.quote: The connecting client IP exceeded the lookup limit.

evidence.proved: arbitrary lookups need the operator's Ipregistry key and answer HTTP 503 without it
evidence.quote: Look up a specific public IPv4 or IPv6 address. Always JSON, even in a browser. Example: /8.8.8.8. Invalid syntax returns 400 INVALID_IP. Private and reserved ranges return 400 RESERVED_IP. Requires the Worker secret IPREGISTRY_API_KEY; otherwise 503 LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE.
Specific-IP lookups (/{ip} and /api/ip/{ip}) are Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400.

evidence.proved: a keyless GET of /8.8.8.8 answered HTTP 200
the answer comes from the Ipregistry data source
the answer carries the documented cache-control header

notes: Free requests: the only published limit is 300 per 60 seconds per caller IP. Rate limit: HTTP 429 with Retry-After 60. Bulk path: none in the HTTP API.
